messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English that is primarily dialogue. Two adult friends are discussing a practical problem, but the conversation should also reveal their personalities and relationship. Use only enough narration to ground the scene. Avoid making every line perfectly witty or overly polished.

“Did you call them?”

“Yes.”

“And?”

“They said they'd call back.”

“When?”

“They didn't say.”

Jordan sighed. “That's helpful.”

“I thought so.”

“You're making fun of me.”

“A little.”

“Good.”

Alex looked at her. “You okay?”

“Yeah.”

“You don't sound okay.”

“I don't like waiting.”

“I know.”

“And I don't like not knowing what's going on.”

“I know that too.”

Jordan rubbed her forehead. “So what do we do?”

“Wait.”

“That is the worst possible answer.”

“Probably.”

“You could at least pretend to have a better one.”

“I could.”

“Well?”

“I've got nothing.”

Jordan laughed despite herself. “Great.”

Alex smiled. “There you go.”

“What?”

“You're laughing.”

“Don't get excited.”

“Too late.”
